cluster_name: Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor deal agreed as US declares mines cleared
event_summary: US Central Command confirmed clearing Iranian sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes in late August 2026. Iran and Oman announced a phased framework for a temporary joint shipping corridor, while Iran's IRGC stated the strait would not reopen unless the US accepted Iran's conditions.
tldr: At the headline layer the Hormuz story splits three ways: US outlets and CGTN lead with Trump's mine-clearing as a decisive military success, Iranian state titles insist Tehran's control is intact and the Oman arrangement falls short of reopening, and Turkey-Egypt-Gulf-diaspora press foregrounds the corridor diplomacy. RT abandons factual framing entirely to relay an Iranian diplomat's attack on Trump's mental fitness — the starkest headline-register departure in the corpus.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to stack three separate victory claims in one title — CENTCOM clearance, Iranian oil at zero, and Trump's 'begging' boast — the most maximalist US-triumph framing in the corpus and absent from centrist US coverage.

Only headline with zero factual content about the mine-clearing or corridor deal; instead relays an Iranian diplomat's charge that Trump has 'Hormuz schizophrenia' — pure rhetorical relay with no news framing of the underlying events.

Only outlet to foreground Trump's explicit military threat against Oman itself ('We'll Bomb Them'), framing US coercion of the neutral mediator rather than pressure on Tehran — a headline angle entirely absent from every other title.

Headline deliberately deflates the corridor announcement ('Oman understanding does not mean Hormuz reopening') while IRNA English simultaneously ran a headline confirming the corridor agreement — revealing a split Iranian state messaging strategy within the same day.

Only headline to frame the Hormuz corridor deal as a step in a larger diplomatic process ('tests path back to Iran-US talks') rather than a standalone agreement — the sole title advertising negotiations-as-process rather than negotiations-as-event.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents a tripartite split: US and Chinese state titles advertise an American military win, Iranian state titles assert unchanged sovereign control and deflate the Oman deal, and regional neutral outlets foreground the corridor diplomacy — the most vivid headline-body divergence candidates are Breitbart (maximalist victory stack) and RT (pure rhetorical attack with no event framing).
